# Supporting sustainable food environments for low income workers in urban Hanoi

We model a decision impact pathway to support sustainable food environments for low income workers in urban Hanoi. The decision is for large companies (i.e. garment factories) to support the establishment of farmstands on campus or connecting farm cooperatives to workers. Each option is compared to a 'do nothing' scenario in terms of how it will influence the outcomes for the company, supporting sustainable food environments and not causing a loss to the company. 

## Simulation of the farmstand intervention options

```{r mcsimulation, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Source our model
source("company_model.R")

# Ensure consistent results with the random number generator
# not for each 'run' of the MC simulation but for 
# consistency each time we run the entire simulation 
set.seed(84)

# Monte Carlo simulation 
source("functions/mcSimulation.R")

company_simulation_results <- mcSimulation(
  estimate = estimate_read_csv("data/company_input.csv"),
  model_function = company_model,
  numberOfModelRuns =  1e4, #run 10,000 times
  functionSyntax = "plainNames"
)

```

### The Net Present Value (i.e. current value of the future benefits). 

Here we plot the distribution for the decision and frame the projected NPV. 

```{r plot_dist_boxplot, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# plot distributions for the two options
source("functions/plot_distributions.R")
Fig_distributions <- plot_distributions(mcSimulation_object = company_simulation_results, 
                   vars = c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm"),
                   old_names = c("decision_farmstand", "decision_connectFarm"),
                   new_names = c("NPV farmstand vs. do nothing", "NPV connect farm vs. do nothing"),
                   method = 'boxplot', 
                   base_size = 11,
                   x_axis_name = "Comparative NPV outcomes over five years (million VND)")

Fig_distributions

ggsave("figures/Fig_distributions.png", width = 15, height = 8, units = "cm") 

```

## Cash flow plot 

```{r combined_cashflow_boxplot, message=FALSE}

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)

# Load simulation results
company_data <- read_csv("results/company_simulation_results.csv")

# Prepare connectFarm data
cashflow_connectFarm <- company_data %>%
  select(starts_with("cashflow_connectFarm")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "CashFlow"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(str_extract(Year, "\\d+")),
    Scenario = "ConnectFarm"
  )

# Prepare farmstand data
cashflow_farmstand <- company_data %>%
  select(starts_with("cashflow_farmstand")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "CashFlow"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(str_extract(Year, "\\d+")),
    Scenario = "FarmStand"
  )

# Combine both
combined_cashflow <- bind_rows(cashflow_connectFarm, cashflow_farmstand)

# Plot boxplot with facets
ggplot(combined_cashflow, aes(x = factor(Year), y = CashFlow, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.color = "gray40", outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "crossbar", width = 0.65, color = "orange", fatten = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Scenario) +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Cash Flow (million VND)"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ConnectFarm" = "steelblue", "FarmStand" = "green")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# Save the combined plot
ggsave("figures/Fig_cashflow_combined_boxplot.png", width = 10, height = 5)

```

## Projection to Latent Structures (PLS)

We use Projection to Latent Structures (PLS) model to assess the correlation strength and direction for model variables and outcome variables. The Partial Least Squares is fitted with the orthogonal scores algorithm with `pls::plsr`.

```{r pls_farmstand}

source("functions/pls_model.R")
pls_result <- pls_model(object = company_simulation_results,
                resultName = names(company_simulation_results$y)[1],  
                                ncomp = 1)
# read in the common input table
input_table <- read.csv("data/company_input.csv")

plot_pls_farmstand <- plot_pls(plsrResults = pls_result, 
                            input_table = input_table, 
                            threshold = 0.9) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_blank(), 
  axis.text.x = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks = element_blank()) + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) + 
  ggtitle("Projection to Latent Structures (PLS)") + 
  annotate(geom="text", x=5, y=2, label="Farmstand")

#For farmstand with formal STEM education
pls_result_connect<- pls_model(object = company_simulation_results,
                  resultName = names(company_simulation_results$y)[2],
                                ncomp = 1)

plot_pls_connect <- plot_pls(plsrResults = pls_result_connect, 
                          input_table = input_table, 
                          threshold = 0.9) + 
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 7)) + 
  annotate(geom="text", x=5, y=2, label="Farm connect")

Fig_pls <- plot_pls_farmstand / plot_pls_connect 

ggsave("figures/Fig_pls.png", width=10, height=4)

Fig_pls
```

## Value of Information

Here we assess value of information with the `multi_EVPI` function. We calculate value of information in the form of Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI).


EVPI for the decision options:

```{r plot_evpi_farmstand}
#Value of information 
source("functions/plot_evpi.R")
plot_evpi_farmstand <- plot_evpi(EVPIresults = evpi,
                            decision_vars = "decision_farmstand",
                            new_names = "Farmstand",
                          input_table = input_table,
                          threshold = 10, 
                          min_evpi = 1) +
theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title.x = element_blank()) +
 scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 25))

```

```{r plot_evpi_connectfarm}

plot_evpi_connectfarm <- plot_evpi(EVPIresults = evpi,
                            decision_vars = "decision_connectFarm",
                            new_names = "Connect farm",
                          input_table = input_table,
                          threshold = 10, 
                          min_evpi = 0.02) +
theme(legend.position = "none")  +
 scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 25))


Fig_evpi <- plot_evpi_farmstand / plot_evpi_connectfarm 

ggsave("figures/Fig_evpi.png", width = 20, height = 10, units = "cm")

Fig_evpi
```

## Input data for the simulations 

### Summary

Here we provide a summary of the intervention options. We do this with a summary table of the simulation results. We show the percentage of missing values as well as the mean, median and standard deviation (SD) for each output of our model simulations. We use the `gt_plt_summary()` from {gtExtras} and with options from {svglite}. The table shows the  name, the plot overview as well as the number of missing values, the mean, median and the standard deviation of the distribution for all variables that were fed into the model from our input table of uncertainty values. 

```{r gtExtras_summary_x, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Subset the outputs from the mcSimulation function (y) to summarize only on the variables that we want.
# names(company_simulation_results$x)
mcSimulation_table_x <- data.frame(company_simulation_results$x[4:7]) #, 21:30, 32:41, 43:70, 73:76)  also of possible interest

 gtExtras::gt_plt_summary(mcSimulation_table_x) 
# a summary table with missing, mean, median and sd

```

The table shows the variable name, the plot overview as well as the number of missing values, the mean, median and the standard deviation of the distribution for variables that calculated in the model.
